customer_jordan: Hi team — a customer report: SSE stream pauses mid-response ~30-40s in, client eventually reconnects and gets a truncated output. Path goes: Cloudflare -> Global Accelerator -> ALB -> targets. Happening for ~3 tenants. Anyone seen similar?

sre_anna: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal curl repro and whether the client shows a socket close or just silence? Also which model/route?

customer_jordan: Repro: `curl -v --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-small' > out.txt`
Behavior: stream emits events for ~30-40s then stops sending any bytes. Connection stays ESTABLISHED from client POV for ~90-120s, then client reconnects automatically and receives truncated/partial result. No immediate 5xx.

support-ops-jim: Quick checklist: capture tcpdump on target and client, ALB access logs, Cloudflare request logs. If ALB idle timeout is 60s that can produce FIN after inactivity. Cloudflare also has a request timeout ~100s for HTTP; GA/NLB combos can complicate TCP behavior.

sre_anna: Added repro steps: 1) `curl --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -v ...` 2) on target: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w sse.pcap port 443` 3) check ALB access logs for `target_processing_time` and `elb_status_code`/`target_status_code`. Share pcap and logs.

eng-ml-raj: From runtime side — we emit small keepalive heartbeats every 15s. If an upstream proxy buffers small chunks (CF or some ALB/NGINX configs) those heartbeats may be coalesced and not forwarded to client quickly, so client-side read can stall until buffer fills or proxy times out. Also if there are TCP window issues (MSS/clamping via GA/NLB) you can see bursts and retransmits.

customer_jordan: Attaching a trimmed tcpdump: shows data arrives at load balancer but then a series of pure ACKs with no payload for ~80s, then retransmits and a spike of data. ALB access log shows request open and no completion; Cloudflare logs show `Origin connection closed` around the same window.

sre_anna: Hypothesis: Cloudflare + GA + ALB is creating a path where small writes are coalesced; combined with ALB idle timeout (60s) we get midstream pause. Two possible fixes: 1) increase ALB idle timeout to > provisioning of longest expected pause (eg 180s) and 2) disable response buffering / enable streaming/cache bypass on CF for that route.

eng-ml-raj: We also have a server-side mitigation: bump min chunk size and force a flush after each event on CF paths. Example config we can toggle per-tenant: 
```
streaming:\n  heartbeat_interval_ms: 15000\n  min_chunk_bytes: 128\n  flush_after_event: true
```
This reduces small writes that proxies might buffer and ensures visible traffic to keep TCP/windows alive. We're testing a patch that aggressively flushes for CF/ALB combos.

support-ops-jim: For a quick customer workaround I asked them to set ALB idle timeout to 180s and create a Cloudflare rule to bypass response buffering for `/v1/stream*`. After that their curl repro no longer pauses.

customer_jordan: Confirmed: after ALB -> 180s + CF bypass the stream remained continuous end-to-end during a 5 minute test. We'll keep monitoring but this looks resolved for now. Thanks! :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary streaming-flush-patch rolled at 2026-03-01T12:02Z — watch SLOs.

sre_anna: Follow-ups: 1) we'll add a diagnostic flag to include `X-Proxy-Chain` header in responses (CF/GA/ALB) so we can quickly see which proxies are on the path. 2) document recommended ALB + Cloudflare streaming settings in the support runbook. 3) engineering to continue validating flush patch.

customer_jordan: appreciated — please ping when doc is up so we can share with customers. :thumbsup:
